title: Nginx as a Reverse Proxy: Fast Setup

scenes.line2: What does a reverse proxy do?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why Nginx pops up in so many interviews? What does it actually do as a reverse proxy?

scenes.label: Proxy
scenes.sub: Nginx forwards client requests to backend servers.
scenes.say: Nginx acts as a middleman, sending client requests to backend servers. That's the essence of a reverse proxy.
Here's the flow: Nginx listens, secures with SSL, forwards traffic to upstream servers, and sets headers to keep host and client info.

scenes.title: Reload Nginx Safely
scenes.say: Always test your config before reloading Nginx. Reload keeps your app running without downtime. Restarting does not.

scenes.question: Why log the X-Forwarded-For header?
scenes.right: To capture the real client IP address, not just the proxy's.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Why log the X-Forwarded-For header? It's not for backend health. It's so you see the real client IP, not just the proxy.
